statement: A straight line commensurable with the side of the sum of two medial areas is the side of the sum of two medial areas.
heath_proof: Let AB be the side of the sum of two medial areas, and CD commensurable with AB; it is to be proved that CD is also the side of the sum of two medial areas. For, since AB is the side of the sum of two medial areas, let it be divided into its straight lines at E; therefore AE, EB are straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial, the rectangle contained by them medial, and furthermore the sum of the squares on AE, EB incommensurable with the rectangle AE, EB. [X. 41] Let the same construction be made as before. We can then prove similarly that CF, FD are also incommensurable in square, the sum of the squares on AE, EB is commensurable with the sum of the squares on CF, FD, and the rectangle AE, EB with the rectangle CF, FD; so that the sum of the squares on CF, FD is also medial, the rectangle CF, FD is medial, and moreover the sum of the squares on CF, FD is incommensurable with the rectangle CF, FD. Therefore CD is the side of the sum of two medial areas.

**Statement:** A straight line commensurable with the side of the sum of two medial areas is the side of the sum of two medial areas.

**Step 1.** Let AB be a side of the sum of two medial areas, and let AB be divided at C so that AC, CB are the two straight lines of which it is composed. Then by the definition of the side of the sum of two medial areas (10.41), AC and CB are incommensurable in square, the sum of the squares on AC and CB is medial, the rectangle contained by AC and CB is medial, and the sum of the squares on AC and CB is incommensurable with the rectangle AC·CB.

**Step 2.** Let DE be commensurable in length with AB. We must show that DE is also a side of the sum of two medial areas.

**Step 3.** Let DE be divided at F such that DF is to FE as AC is to CB (6.12). Then since AC is to CB as DF is to FE, it follows that AB is to DE as AC is to DF and as CB is to FE (5.12, 5.16, 5.18). Since AB is commensurable with DE, it follows that AC is commensurable with DF and CB is commensurable with FE (10.11).

**Step 4.** Since AC is commensurable with DF, the squares on AC and DF are commensurable (10.11). Similarly, since CB is commensurable with FE, the squares on CB and FE are commensurable. Therefore the sum of the squares on AC and CB is commensurable with the sum of the squares on DF and FE (10.12, 10.15).

**Step 5.** Now the sum of the squares on AC and CB is medial. Since the sum of the squares on DF and FE is commensurable with a medial area, the sum of the squares on DF and FE is also medial (10.23 applied to areas, that is, an area commensurable with a medial area is medial, by 10.15 and the definition of medial D10.1.4).

**Step 6.** Since AC is to CB as DF is to FE, the rectangle AC·CB is to the rectangle DF·FE as the square on AC is to the square on DF (6.16). But the square on AC is commensurable with the square on DF (from Step 4). Therefore the rectangle AC·CB is commensurable with the rectangle DF·FE (10.11).

**Step 7.** Now the rectangle AC·CB is medial. Since the rectangle DF·FE is commensurable with a medial area, the rectangle DF·FE is also medial.

**Step 8.** Since the sum of the squares on AC and CB is incommensurable with the rectangle AC·CB, and the sum of the squares on DF and FE is commensurable with the sum of the squares on AC and CB (Step 4), and the rectangle DF·FE is commensurable with the rectangle AC·CB (Step 6), it follows that the sum of the squares on DF and FE is incommensurable with the rectangle DF·FE (10.13).

**Step 9.** Since AC is to CB as DF is to FE, and AC and CB are incommensurable in square, DF and FE are also incommensurable in square (10.11).

**Step 10.** Therefore DF and FE are two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial (Step 5), the rectangle contained by them medial (Step 7), and the sum of the squares on them incommensurable with the rectangle contained by them (Step 8). Therefore their sum DE is the side of the sum of two medial areas (10.41).

**Step 11.** Hence a straight line commensurable with the side of the sum of two medial areas is itself also the side of the sum of two medial areas. Q.E.D.
